plates.title: WHAT THE NUMBER DID NOT SEE
plates.subtitle: Entropy
plates.summary: Tiles change neighbours while the tally stays. Another arrangement can hold the same inventory and another view.
plates.focus: Categorical shares omit order; visible displacement and rubble are different accounts.
panels: Here, choose a pair of neighbouring colours before touching a button.
At long ledger desk, student points at adjacent different-coloured tiles; many coloured tiles in retained row, ten small count bars on panel.
The tiles glide into ten blocks, one per symbol; the bars hold their places.
Matched temporal views AS DRAWN / SORTED, SAME colour quantities reordered into colour blocks. Ten histogram bars identical in both. A cropped enlarged old excerpt stays on desk front.
It has stayed too.

Companion looks at SAME H in both views, label H same. Do not invent exact sample value. Student notices changed neighbours. Tiny inset two arrangements with equal red/blue counts, different adjacent pairs.
The ruler has changed with the thing it measures.

CONTRAST weighted sample dominates first bar. Small inset counts2/4 and4/8 both scaled maximum to same displayheight, clearly SCHEMATIC separate example, not live sample. Numerical counts remain distinct.
The fallen stone is still here.
Four-column pale lintel ruin, top capital removed and arranged in rubble below, other stones retained. No dust disappearance, no thermodynamic gauge. Person on permanent museum floor.
What was a boundary now lets you see across it.
Museum wall top courses dismantled, stones on ground; low edgecourse and floor retain support. Visitor sees through opening, ruined gallery arrangement with no entropy meter measuring stones.
plates.footer: What does a count of stones tell us about what they can still hold?

plates.title: THE SET BEFORE THE CHOICE
plates.subtitle: Remove
plates.summary: Grey cubes remain unavailable. An empty slot keeps its address; a missing floor cell also withdraws support.
plates.focus: Filter, draw and removal are separate; support is an additional instruction.

Pedestal square board EXACTLY 8x8 cubes; central4x4 amber, outer48 grey. Adult points at outergrey. Clear topview inset may ensure counting, no perspective losing rows.
the draw is made before the deletion.
Same board one amber cube red, rest amber/grey. Insets RED then EMPTY addressplate retained. Red not another cube arriving. REMOVE ONE pushbutton.
The final shape was never in doubt: the square you counted at the start, emptied.
After16removals central4x4 slots EMPTY with pale slotplates visible, grey border unchanged. Address grid stays8x8. Visitor sees chosen square absence.
An absence has become part of the next choice.
Two glass hoppers eight numberedslots each. LEFT selected2 returns, resultcopy2 retained beneath; RIGHT selected2 staysout, its slotempty. No extra physical2 inside right.
The gap is now something your body can fall through.

Visitor ON permanent dark apron beside glass-framed amber floor over fire basin. One redcell about to disappear; separate AFTER cutaway gap through support. No floating ungrounded feet or collision barrier over hole.
Walking makes a choice happen; it does not tell the choice where to land.

plates.title: WHEN A MARK BECOMES A WALL
plates.subtitle: 10 PRINT
plates.summary: Two diagonals become a plane, a floor and solid walls. An arrangement can close a figure and refuse a body.
plates.focus: Layout, bias, material and crop decide what binary draws can become.
panels: Something that fits inside one character has acquired room for a body.
Student stands between tall diagonal slabs near entrance, diagonal printscreen farwall. Walls actualsolid, shoulder-scale passages.
The maze has become stripes.
Printer two framed snapshots EVEN / ONE DIRECTION: mixeddiagonal small squaregrid vs allparallel diagonals. BIAS+ button near; no claim every unbiased sample has equalcount.
The field becomes a single column.
SEMICOLON OFF makesonevertical column of same seeded diagonal signs. Paired inset planar4x4 / column16, exactly same row-major signs. No encloseddiamonds in column.
One tiny character has given the other characters another way to meet.
Simple separate2x2 diagram four diagonals formingdiamond: top row / then backslash, lower row backslash then /. Endpoints at centres of outeredges. This is a possible configuration, not all marks.
They give the eye a contour without giving the body a boundary.
Low halfmetre diagonalridges onfloor; visitorwalks among them. No huge solidfloorbarriers. Screen paused STEP button nearby.
The same connection that completes a figure can keep a body outside it.
Tall slabs enclose small diamond room with NOentrance. Visitors outside. Separate nearby open corridor, not forced doorway in closeddiamond.
plates.footer: The marks alone cannot tell us which world we have made.
